trust_decision.summary: One decision, made in the frps SSH tunnel gateway's per-channel request loop: the length prefix of an SSH 'exec' channel request is trusted and used to slice the payload. `end := 4 + binary.BigEndian.Uint32(req.Payload[:4])` is uint32 arithmetic, so a prefix of 0xFFFFFFFF wraps end to 3 and `req.Payload[4:end]` panics in a bare goroutine, killing frps. No authentication is needed in the default config (authorizedKeysFile empty => NoClientAuth).

landing_point.why: The summary names the SSH tunnel gateway and an integer overflow; the only integer arithmetic on a client-supplied value in the gateway is `4 + binary.BigEndian.Uint32(req.Payload[:4])` in handleNewChannel, immediately followed by a slice indexed by it (server.go:319). The package is only three files, so this is the first and only place to look.

fix_sites.entry_point: frps SSH tunnel gateway TCP listener (sshTunnelGateway.bindPort, server/service.go:279-285) -> Gateway.Run (pkg/ssh/gateway.go:105) -> handleConn -> TunnelServer.Run (pkg/ssh/server.go:87) -> waitForwardAddrAndExtraPayload -> handleNewChannel (spawned per client-opened channel, pkg/ssh/server.go:226)
fix_sites.module_kind: server-side SSH protocol handler / gateway (network entry point, no HTTP route or CLI command)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site and no O8 route exists; the only dismissal a solver could reach for is that the crash needs the gateway run in its documented default (authorizedKeysFile empty => unauthenticated, doc/ssh_tunnel_gateway.md:144,148), i.e. that it is a deployment choice rather than a code defect.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A legitimate exec payload is a full cobra command line ('tcp --remote-port N --proxy-name x', 'tcpmux --mux=httpconnect --custom-domain d') that is split on single spaces and handed to cobra; and every channel request including a rejected one must still be answered with Reply(true, nil) on the channel that is also the proxy data path. An over-broad fix that rejects payloads with option-like tokens, caps the payload length, only accepts a fixed token set, or replies false / closes the channel on a parse failure breaks the documented client usage and the e2e tunnel cases.

O6_input_shapes: canonical RFC 4254 section 6.5 form: 4-byte big-endian length prefix followed by the command string
payload shorter than the 4-byte prefix (3 bytes)
declared length greater than the remaining bytes (prefix 2, one data byte)
length prefix 0xFFFFFFFF, for which 4+prefix wraps to 3 in uint32 arithmetic

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second per-request parser in the same request loop (e.g. a 'shell'/'pty-req' payload reader, or an inbound 'direct-tcpip' channel-open parser for ssh -L support) that hand-slices the request payload bytes
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This file already hand-writes RFC 4254 payloads (tcpipForward at server.go:50-53, forwardedTCPPayload at server.go:56-62, ssh.Marshal at server.go:352) instead of relying on library helpers, and handleNewChannel special-cases one request type; a maintainer adding a second one would copy the surrounding style, giving a HOW-type sibling one function away from the landing point.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: validation performed at the token layer instead of the byte layer: code that indexes strings.Split(extraPayload, " ") results (or inspects args[i] for a flag value) without a length guard
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The payload's identity is re-derived here by a separator split and then re-parsed by cobra with WordSepNormalizeFunc (server.go:260,275) and '='-form flags used by the e2e client (test/e2e/v1/features/ssh_tunnel.go:134); a maintainer adding a check on this side would be validating argv, not the length prefix, so a byte-level fix at the sink does not carry over.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a frame reader on the main frps control connection that trusts the client-supplied uint32 frame length (allocate or slice from it before the bound check)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: wire v2 is new 2026 code with a hand-rolled 8-byte header and a 32-bit length taken straight off the wire (wire.go:68-76); the same 'client controls the length, we slice with it' mechanism lives two packages away from pkg/ssh on the most exposed port, and the current maxFramePayloadSize guard reads as an obvious thing to reorder or drop when adding a new frame kind.

O9_family: improper validation of an array index / integer overflow (CWE-129, CWE-190) on a length-prefixed protocol field, yielding an out-of-bounds slice panic in an unrecovered goroutine

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.25.0 (go.mod:3); Makefile targets build/test; modules from the proxy (go.sum present, no vendor dir)
O10_build.project_tests: test/e2e/v1/features/ssh_tunnel.go has five ginkgo cases (tcp, http, https, tcpmux, stcp) that start frps with sshTunnelGateway.bindPort and drive the gateway through test/e2e/pkg/ssh/client.go over 127.0.0.1; pkg/ssh has no test file at the pinned commit - pkg/ssh/server_test.go is created by the fix (fix.diff:216).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: keep the hand-rolled parse and just stop the crash - a defer recover() in handleNewChannel, or rejecting only the exact 0xFFFFFFFF prefix from the report - leaving the length prefix unvalidated for every other wrapped value

out_of_scope_notes: The same commit bumps golib 0.7.2->0.8.0 and x/crypto, x/net, x/sync, x/sys (fix.diff:30-157) and adds a staticcheck SA1019 exclusion for pkg/util/vhost/http.go, which reads as h2c migration collateral for a separate advisory; not pursued.

test/e2e/pkg/ssh/client.go:44-54 is an in-repo producer of the same length-prefixed exec payload (ssh.Marshal of command{Cmd string}, note the different field name from the fix's execPayload{Command}); it is test code and was not changed by the fix.

The only SSH implementation in the tree is golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, used in exactly pkg/ssh/gateway.go, pkg/ssh/server.go and test/e2e/pkg/ssh/client.go, so no second SSH server exists to carry a sibling of this sink.
unverified: Repository size was not measured (no shell available in this session), so tiny_repo could not be ruled in or out; frp carries e2e tests, docs and a frontend asset package, so under 5 MB of source is unlikely.

Whether golang.org/x/crypto/ssh.Unmarshal rejects payloads with trailing bytes after the declared string was not checked against the dependency source (it is not in the tree); the fix therefore may or may not change behaviour for payloads where the declared length is shorter than the buffer, which the old code silently accepted (server.go:316-319).

The fix's new unit test marshals execPayload directly (fix.diff:246) rather than going through the e2e client, so parity with the in-repo producer at test/e2e/pkg/ssh/client.go:54 is asserted by inspection only.

Whether a panic in the goroutine spawned at pkg/ssh/server.go:226 is ever recovered: the only recover() calls in the tree are server/control.go:577 and pkg/util/net/udp.go:71,220, none on this path, so frps exits; this was read, not executed.
